result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.largest_component_size()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the size of the largest connected component. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L15071-L15110){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.largest_component_size() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} For undirected graphs, finds the largest connected component. For directed graphs, finds the largest weakly connected component. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes in the largest connected component. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Get the size of the largest component: ::: {#e77b1733 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_full_graph(5) # Returns 5 - all nodes in single component graph.largest_component_size() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 5 ``` ::: ::: After removing nodes, the component may fragment: ::: {#4857e505 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_full_graph(5) percolated = graph.node_percolation(q=0.5, seed=23) # Returns size of largest component (may be smaller after percolation) percolated.largest_component_size() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
